items.title: Terminal sessions persist ref-only identity and status
items.statement: A terminal session record is keyed per project and session, requires pane, status, shell-profile, cwd, timestamps, and redaction fields, and may carry nullable exit, last-command, and process-identity refs.

items.title: Runtime must revalidate active process identity
items.statement: Stored session identity and status are historical replay inputs; reuse of an active process identity requires runtime revalidation.

items.title: Terminal session transition contract is absent
items.statement: The schema enumerates starting, running, closed, detached, and restore_required, but this window does not define legal transitions, triggering events, concurrency rules, or field invariants such as when exit_code or process_identity_ref must be present or cleared.
items.impact: Independent builders can produce incompatible lifecycle behavior and disagree about whether a persisted session can be resumed or must be restored.
items.builder_discretion: Transition graph, event-to-transition mapping, idempotency, and status-dependent field rules remain open.

dimension_assessments.summary: Materialized terminal replay behaviors and deferred projection rebuild/restore behaviors are explicit.
The window defines panel, session, command, analytics, goal, GUI-state, and recovery projection capabilities, with deferred groups clearly labeled.
Key shapes, required and optional fields, schema constraints, encodings, and producer/consumer edges provide structural input/output contracts.
Structural schemas are concrete for materialized terminal families, but semantic cross-field, reference, and projection-consistency contracts remain incomplete.
Session and command status enums exist without legal transition graphs, triggering events, or status-dependent field invariants.
The excerpt distinguishes runtime authority from panel and command replay, identifies goal events and receipts as authoritative, and limits stale projections to inspection.
Each family provides an owner_doc or deferred_owner; the terminal families share storage-plan ownership.

Terminal GUI, Runtime Artifacts, tool/debug surfaces, GitHub/browser surfaces, orchestrator, goal views, certification readers, usage widgets, dashboard, source control, notifications, executor, and restore flows are enumerated.
Panel visibility/docking are explicit presentation truth; deferred GUI families restore presentation without launch authority, and stale GUI projections are inspectable only.
Runtime revalidation and recovery anchor requirements are explicit, but transition failures, scrub failures, compaction failures, and partial projection rebuild recovery are not.
No-secret and sensitive-metadata rules are strong, but scrubbed-ref enforcement and export-masking semantics lack operational contracts and test vectors.
Producers and rebuild sources are named, but event ordering, duplicate handling, invalidation, checkpoint atomicity, and stale-read signaling are absent.
Retention and compaction intentions exist without numeric bounds, scheduling, anchor precedence, or deletion failure/retry behavior.
No row-size, cardinality, scan, latency, rebuild, or write-amplification acceptance bounds appear in the window.
Migration direction and namespace constraints are named, but executable transforms, source-version detection, rollback, and idempotency are unspecified.
JSON-schema constraints provide structural oracles, but lifecycle, migration, security, performance, and projection-consistency fixtures or executable pass criteria are missing.
Builders retain consequential choices over state machines, ref enforcement, retention, migration, projection consistency, export masking, and performance budgets.
Consequential referenced policies and stale-state criteria are not defined within the authorized window; exact behavior therefore remains unknown here.
